options.reason: Bars make the discrete annual death totals straightforward to compare year by year.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how many pedestrians were killed in each calendar year, using the sum of the pedestrian-fatality count recorded on crash rows. Bars support direct comparison of yearly totals; the chart does not break those deaths down by borough, location, or crash circumstances.

options.denominator: None; annual count of pedestrian deaths
options.reason: A line chart makes the year-to-year direction and fluctuations in the requested counts easy to follow.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the annual-count question while emphasizing how pedestrian deaths changed over time: the count was highest in 2013 at 176 and lowest in 2020 at 101, then it fluctuated through 2025. It is defensible for showing a time sequence, but it does not explain the causes of those changes or identify where deaths occurred.
